Feature

Image of the Child

By Cindy McGaha

The Child Development Laboratory (CDL) is a community of practice that engages in deep reflection and study of the work of children. We strive to understand the theories and ideas that children create through collecting children's words and actions in the context of play. For the coming year, the CDL will be exploring Image of the Child. Image of the Child encompasses "what people believe, understand, and assume about the role of children in education and society. This image includes how people think about children's capabilities, development, motivations, purpose and agency. Social, cultural, and historical experiences influence a person's image of the child" (Martalock, 2012, p. 3). The Reggio Emilia approach (our guiding philosophy) utilizes this concept as a framework for guiding the ways in which we engage with children.

In the coming year, we hope to engage our community in an exploration of how each of us sees children and how that influences the ways in which we engage with children. We will share observations and reflections by the children, families, Work College students and CDL staff. Our goal in this exploration is to challenge ourselves in truly seeing children and revealing children's thinking and learning. Pedagogical documentation will be shared throughout the year. We welcome members of the community to engage in reflection with us on the true competence of children and how we can create spaces where children's competence can be revealed and encouraged.

Announcement

Coming Soon: Automatic Waitlists!

By Sarah Adams, Executive Director of General Education and Interim Dean of Curriculum

For spring 2027 registration, we will begin using automatic waitlists! Turning on our existing automatic waitlist feature will allow us to gauge student interest to inform decisions about adding sections, give priority to students who are closest to graduation, and support fairer access to seats as they become available. Faculty will continue to grant overrides for prerequisites and class standing restrictions, but we'll use a new process for courses that have reached capacity. We'll share full details soon!

Feature

Please Join Us for Convo!

By Sarah Adams, Executive Director of General Education and Interim Dean of Curriculum

You're invited to join 1,000+ of your favorite students in Phelps Stokes Chapel each week for Convocation.

The benefits of attending Convo are many:

  • You can literally "meet students where they are" while modeling what lifelong learning looks like
  • You'll have something new to talk about at your next department or committee meeting
  • You have a built-in excuse for not having meetings, answering emails, or grading papers for a whole hour each week

This year's Convo series has already been off to a great start, with a rollicking concert from the legendary Tee Dee Young (during which a couple dozen of his new Berean friends joined him on stage!) and a fascinating lecture from Dr. Kavitha Arur about how black holes are definitely NOT space vacuums.

Coming up, we'll host:

  • Sept. 24, 3:00 PM: Ato Andoh, CEO of GCS Fibers
  • Oct. 1, 8:00 PM: Ukrainian Village Voices, Choir
  • Oct. 8, 3:00 PM: Taylor Fellows Showcase
  • Oct. 22, 3:00 PM: Andrew Aydin & Cory Vaillancourt, contributors to Islands in the Sky: A People's History of Hurricane Helene
  • Nov. 5, 3:00 PM: Brian Christian, author of The Alignment Problem: Machine Learning and Human Values
  • Nov. 12, 8:00 PM: Los Juanos, Indie-Regional Mexicano Band

Announcement

AI Ready Webinars: AI as an Accessibility Tool

The next topic in the AI Ready webinar series is AI as an Accessibility Tool, a three-part series held on three Thursdays in October, all from 2:00 to 3:00 PM Eastern: Oct. 8, 15, and 22. Each one-hour session looks at real-world use cases, ethical questions, and institutional strategies for using AI to deliver accommodations faster, personalize access, and remove barriers before they get in the way of learning.

There is no cost to participate, and everyone is welcome. You can register at the registration site.

Anyone who would rather watch with others can join us in the Legacy Training Room in the Legacy Building. If there is enough interest, we will reserve the hour after each webinar for a group discussion about AI at Berea College. Let Rob Smith, Berea's AI Ready contact, know if you would like to take part.

Announcement

Talk with Remi Kalir

By Joe Murphy, Director of Educational Development

Remi Kalir

Thursday, September 24th · 12:00 PM · Hutchins Room in Dining, or online

Pressing Prompts is an open collection of activities, resources, and pedagogical guidance for higher education instructors who are interested in bringing AI ethics into their classrooms. The project invites educators and their students to embrace inquiry and complexity as we collectively navigate our relationships with AI.

Join us for an online discussion with Remi Kalir, Associate Director of Faculty Development and Applied Research at Duke University and one of the authors of Pressing Prompts, about how the collection was built and how faculty are using it.

You can join online or at the Hutchins Room in Dining. (Lunch will be provided if you attend in person.) RSVP here.

Announcement

Share Your Expertise: Media Relations Seeks Subject Matter Experts

Berea College's Media Relations office is launching a new initiative to identify faculty and staff members who may be interested in serving as subject matter experts for media opportunities.

A subject matter expert (SME) is someone with specialized knowledge, experience, research, or professional expertise in a particular area who can help inform the public through interviews with journalists, podcasts, radio programs, television news outlets and other media. Examples might include expertise in Appalachian studies, education, sustainability, economics, religion, health and wellness, college access, labor programs, social justice, agriculture, history, student success, or other academic and professional fields.

When newsworthy topics arise, colleges and universities are often asked to provide expert perspectives that help audiences better understand current events and important issues. By building a database of willing experts, Berea College can more effectively share the knowledge and experiences of our community while increasing awareness of the College's mission and impact.

If you are interested in being considered for future media opportunities, please complete this form.

Please note that expertise submitted should be related to subjects that would be appropriate for a representative of Berea College to discuss publicly. Inclusion in the database does not guarantee media interviews, and participation in any future media opportunity will always be voluntary. The Media Relations Office will work with potential experts to determine whether a specific request is a good fit and can provide guidance and support before interviews.

Thank you for considering this opportunity to help share Berea College's stories, expertise and mission with a broader audience.

If you have any questions, please reach out to Jodi Whitaker at whitakerj7@berea.edu or (859) 338-7917.
